ambiguity: 1) 2026 parameters: indexing the §17052(o)(2) amount for 2026 with the 3.4% June 2025 to June 2026 CCPI rate, which was published after the 2026-07-03 freeze, gives a CalEITC of about $105 instead of about $95. The reference matches the parameters that were published before the freeze. 2) If the $8,089 employer-sponsored insurance premium were read as a pre-tax cafeteria-plan salary reduction, AGI and earned income would drop by $8,089 and the credit would be much larger. The prompt does not say this and tells us not to infer it. 3) The 85% adjustment factor must be re-specified in each annual Budget Act. I assume the 2026 Budget Act kept 85%, as every act since 2015 has, but I did not find the 2026 text.

computation:
1) Earned income: wages $17,443 minus the $2,778 traditional 401(k) deferral, which is excluded from gross income, = $14,665. Roth 401(k) deferrals are not excluded. CA conforms. Under IRC §32(c)(2), as adopted by R&TC §17052, earned income is wages includible in gross income. The $8,089 ESI premium is not stated to be a pre-tax salary reduction, so I do not infer one.
2) AGI: $14,665 + $8,000 taxable 403(b) distributions - $130 traditional IRA deduction = $22,535. The deduction is allowed because MAGI is far below the active-participant phaseout. CA AGI is the same, since CA conforms on all three items. The disability exception to the 10% early-distribution tax does not affect AGI.
3) CalEITC eligibility: R&TC §17052 replaces the federal 25-64 age test with age 18, so a 28-year-old without children qualifies. There is no disqualified (investment) income: pension or 403(b) distributions are not on the IRC §32(i)(2) list, and bank interest is unlisted, so 0. Earned income is positive.
4) Regular CalEITC under §17052(b): 7.65% x 85% adjustment factor, with the phase-in and phaseout both at the 2025 threshold of $4,661. It reaches 0 at about $9,322, so it is $0 at both EI and AGI. That triggers §17052(o): credit percentage 5.43% on the (o)(2) earned income amount ($4,334 in 2019). That amount is indexed under (o)(4)(A) and R&TC §17041(h) with CCPI rates of 1.4%, 4.4%, 8.3%, 3.1%, 3.3% and 3.0%, giving about $4,969 in 2022 and $5,451 in 2025. The phaseout percentage was recalculated so the credit is 0 at $30,000 in 2022: 0.0543 x 4,969 / (30,000 - 4,969) ≈ 1.0779%. Under (o)(4)(B) that percentage carries forward. This is consistent with FTB's published 2025 limit of $32,900.
5) The credit uses the greater of AGI or earned income under IRC §32(a)(2)(B), adopted by §17052(a). The FTB 3514 worksheet does the same: it looks up both EI and AGI and takes the smaller credit.
- 2025 parameters at AGI $22,535: 0.85 x [0.0543 x 5,451 - 0.010779 x (22,535 - 5,451)] = 0.85 x [295.99 - 184.15] = 0.85 x 111.84 ≈ $95.07.
- Same parameters at EI $14,665: ≈ $167.
- The smaller is about $95. The $50-bracket table midpoint gives about $95.15.
6) 2026 amounts: the 2026 CalEITC table and indexed amounts were not published before 2026-07-03. The 2026 indexing uses the June 2025 to June 2026 CCPI change (3.4%, standard deduction $5,900), which could only be known after June 2026 data. The latest values published at the freeze were the 2025 ones: $32,900 limit and $302 maximum without children. Applying 3.4% gives an EI amount of about $5,636 and a credit of 0.85 x [306.03 - 0.010779 x 16,899] ≈ $105.
7) Other CA refundable credits:
- Young Child Tax Credit: none, no child under 6.
- Foster Youth Tax Credit: none, status not listed so false.
- Renter's credit: nonrefundable, so excluded.
Total refundable state credits ≈ $95 (about $105 with post-freeze 2026 indexing). The consensus of $0 wrongly applied the federal childless cutoff or ignored the §17052(o) extension to about $30,000 indexed.
definition_reading: One single filer and one CA tax unit. 'Total refundable state individual income tax credits' means CA refundable PIT credits: CalEITC, Young Child Tax Credit and Foster Youth Tax Credit. Only CalEITC applies. It is about $95 because the §17052(o) extended phaseout runs to about $32,900 and is measured on the greater of AGI ($22,535) or earned income. The nonrefundable renter's credit is excluded.
